title: 37 LISD students earn College Board National Recognition honors
excerpt: Thirty-seven Laredo ISD students from Cigarroa, Martin, Nixon and Garcia Early College high schools earned National First-Generation and National Hispanic Recognition Awards from the College Board.
content:
Thirty-seven Laredo ISD students have earned national recognition from the College Board for their academic achievement, the district announced.

The students, from Cigarroa, Martin, Nixon and Hector J. Garcia Early College high schools, earned the National First-Generation Recognition Award and the National Hispanic Recognition Award. The honors recognize strong academic performance and help students share their achievements with colleges and scholarship programs looking to recruit them.

To qualify, students must have a GPA of 3.5 or higher, PSAT scores in the top 10 percent of test takers in the state, or a score of 3 or higher on two or more AP exams in ninth and tenth grade, along with meeting the programs' eligibility criteria.

Isabella Mendoza, a junior at Garcia Early College High School and a National Hispanic Recognition Award recipient, said she was thrilled to be nominated and receive the award, knowing the hardships her family has gone through to give her generation more opportunities. She said she is grateful and that the recognition gives her many opportunities to showcase her heritage. Mendoza plans to study criminal justice at St. Mary's University in San Antonio, with a dream of becoming a lawyer specializing in criminal law and eventually opening her own firm in Laredo.

Jedidiah Fipps, a senior at Cigarroa High School and a multiple-time recipient of the recognition, said he feels proud to share the honor with his family and peers. Fipps has enlisted in the United States Marine Corps and hopes to become a member of the U.S. Marine Band. He also plans to attend Texas State University to study music education.

Cindy Dominguez, LISD's director of guidance and counseling and at-risk population, said the district takes immense pride in the students' commitment and aspirations. She said the district has seen a consistent rise in the number of qualifying students over the course of the recognition program, a testament to their dedication to college preparatory assessments, strong academic records and leadership.

The honorees from Cigarroa High School are Miriam Bahena, Gael Esquivel, Jedidiah Fipps, Kevin Frayde, David Gonzalez, Christopher Jasso, Kevyn Palomares and Aiden Rodriguez Carrero. From Garcia Early College High School: Alessandra Barberena, Caleb Benavides, Jaqueline Ciriaco, Richard Deschampe, Amador Flores III, Mikayla Flores, Miranda Galvan, Giorgy Guzman, Melina Hernandez, Isabella Mendoza, Gina Montoya, Yullet Parra, Marcos Rodriguez, Zachary Smith and Jasmine Vasquez. From Martin High School: Gabriel Benavides, Keyla Deleon, Natalie Gonzalez, Jesus Martinez and Briana Morales. From Nixon High School: Vanessa Alba, Veronica Cadena, Sayuri Garcia, Maya Lopez, Diego Marines, Mathew Ramon and Zoe Sifuentes.

Sources: Laredo Independent School District, “Laredo ISD students earn College Board National Recognition honors” (Nov. 2026).
